reviews.text:
I came here for an MRI scan on the recommendation of my family doctor.

The clinic was clean, and the doctor was very professional, so I felt at ease leaving my child in their care.

My baby underwent surgery for hydrocephalus at two months old, and we were told that survival was only about five years, but he stayed by our side until he was 15 years and 3 months old. We are all so grateful to this hospital for the surgery and the kind and thorough care we received afterward. It's a wonderful hospital!

Thank you very much.

We express our heartfelt gratitude.
I am truly grateful for the trustworthy and convincing explanation I received. Now it's just a matter of sorting out my own feelings.

It's a nice hospital, and they seem to do thorough examinations.

However, something feels off...

It seems like they're only looking to see if it's cancer or not. That's the only explanation I was given.

I can't say for sure since I haven't received the detailed test results yet, but I wasn't even informed that they were doing those tests.

Well, it's different from my usual hospital.

But the test fees are so expensive.

Without insurance, treatment is impossible...

My dog ​​had a fractured toe and needed surgery. The cost was approximately 600,000 yen (including tax).

On the day of the surgery, I was called in midway through for an explanation. "When we administered the anesthesia, his breathing stopped." What? "He's breathing again now." What? Are you trying to kill my precious pet? Of course, I stopped the surgery. He was hospitalized for one day, and I picked him up the next day to settle the bill. Approximately 120,000 yen. What? They almost killed my dog, but still took my money – a top-notch hospital with third-rate doctors, and I would not recommend it.

When I took my dog ​​in for the examination, they were very polite. They said they would contact my regular vet with the results, and that my vet would contact me in a week. I waited and waited, but no contact came, so I called my vet, who said they hadn't heard anything from the VR Center. When I checked with the VR Center, they said they had forgotten to tell the owner that they would contact me. I was really disappointed by how carelessly they treated the situation. From my perspective, I was anxious about the endoscopy, CT scan, and X-rays, and I paid a high price for my dog's sake, and I was worried every day about whether there was anything wrong. In the end, they did call me to tell me the results, but they hung up saying, "We have an appointment, so we can't talk for long." This is the first time I've ever written a review like this, but if you don't hear back from them for a while, you should contact them as soon as possible.

The consultation was handled by a nurse, and I barely spoke to the veterinarian. After a short examination, I received an explanation before the tests, but the lack of communication with the veterinarian made me anxious. The test results were ultimately unsatisfactory, leaving me with questions. I had taken risks to have the tests done to get a definitive diagnosis, yet I still felt uneasy. Shouldn't veterinarians communicate more with pet owners? Perhaps this is just the case with veterinarians in that particular department. Ultimately, I sought a second opinion at a different hospital specializing in neurosurgery. Their explanation was much more convincing.

While imaging is certainly important, shouldn't veterinarians listen more to what pet owners, who see their animals every day, have to say? Don't you think communication with pet owners is especially important because animals can't speak?

There are two ophthalmologists, but they don't coordinate with each other. They seem to take turns taking days off, but on the day the attending veterinarian is off, they do nothing even if a patient's post-operative condition suddenly deteriorates. They have absolutely no sense of responsibility as a hospital, simply because the patient isn't their own. This is a hospital you should use with the understanding that there's no benefit other than the presence of expensive medical equipment. Furthermore, the receptionist acts as if she represents the entire hospital, giving orders in a very assertive manner. To put it mildly, she comes across as arrogant. Overall, I think this is a veterinary hospital that lacks hospitality.

I visited this clinic for a CT scan of my dog, referred by my regular veterinarian.

Since it's by appointment only, I was seen on time. Although I arrived a little early at this unfamiliar place, the parking lot and waiting room were spacious enough, and there was even a TV, so I was able to relax while waiting.

The examination process involved a nurse carefully listening to my dog's symptoms, followed by a veterinarian's examination, and then the CT scan. The hour-long wait during the scan was manageable; I was able to comfortably wait in the car or waiting room.

The test results revealed my dog's condition was worse than I had anticipated, and I was so shocked that I cried. The veterinarian explained everything very kindly and thoroughly.

Thank you so much for your compassionate support.

Some of you reading this may be feeling anxious as you read this review. I was also very anxious at the time, but I'm posting this in the hope that it might put your mind at ease.

A year ago, my 5-year-old Yorkshire Terrier was diagnosed with a portosystemic shunt at my regular vet, and I was referred to Dr. Une to perform the surgery.

The pre-operative explanation was very thorough and easy to understand, and during hospitalization, they sent me videos via LINE every day, so I was able to see how my beloved dog was doing and felt at ease.

Now, a year after the surgery, there has been no recurrence, and he is doing very well. The cost is certainly not cheap, but the skill and peace of mind it provides are well worth it, and I am truly glad I chose him. I am deeply grateful.

For those of you reading this review with similar anxieties, Dr. Une is a doctor you can trust. I hope this is helpful in some way.

My beloved cat developed megacolon, and after being referred by our regular veterinarian, we had surgery performed at NeoVets.

Since she's almost 15 years old, I was worried about continuing with medical treatment, but I thought that continuing manual disimpaction and hospital visits would be too much of a burden on her, and since she was physically able to withstand the surgery, I decided to go ahead with it.

The surgery was successful, but for a while afterward, her recovery wasn't very good, and she wasn't passing the soft stools she should have, so we went back to the vet. Even then, they were very kind and attentive during our consultation.

As a result, although she's still taking medication, she's now able to defecate steadily on her own!

Also, thanks to continuing IV fluids at home for a while, her kidney values, which were originally poor, have returned to normal, and all her other values ​​are also normal; she's in a very healthy state!

After the surgery, I was very anxious about whether it was really the right decision, but thanks to the surgery, I can see my cat healthy again, and I'm truly grateful.

During her hospitalization, they kept me updated on her condition every day via LINE, and they were very kind and attentive when I visited.

They provide a price estimate beforehand. It was more expensive than average, but I was able to afford it because my insurance covered it.
I don't think I'll need to go again unless I get a serious illness...
Thank you so much, Dr. Morishita and all the nurses.

P.S.
I'm currently able to have a bowel movement every day without taking any medication!

My regular vet said the cause was unknown, so I went to this clinic for a second opinion, desperately hoping they might find something... but all they did was listen to the previous test results and history, and they said, "You've already had so much done, there's nothing more we can do. If you want more tests, you should go to your regular vet." !

I was told, "Just go to your regular vet right now," even though I'd come all this way, and I couldn't believe it.

They even said, "It's not good to get second opinions or opinions from different hospitals, even with human illnesses," but is that really true?

Even within the same hospital, different veterinarians say different things, and sometimes a different doctor might notice something for the first time, so I don't think that's true at all.

This is a secondary care advanced medical center, yet they have that opinion...

They apparently listened to the previous tests and history beforehand, but if there's nothing they can do, shouldn't they have known that from the beginning? They should have told me that when I made the appointment.

Why did I bring him here?

Why did I fast him?

Do you understand the feelings of the pet owner who brought their pet in?

I didn't just go there to chat!

Furthermore, the conversation often went off on a tangent without really listening to what I was saying, and I wasted time on pointless chatter where I thought, "That's not what I meant!" The words were polite, but what was actually said was condescending.

I was so angry and sad I almost cried, but I held back.

After listening to my story, they said, "Go to your regular vet for the tests," but then they charged me 4000 yen for the initial consultation and 6000 yen for the specialist consultation, totaling 10000 yen!

I really don't understand it.

If you're making an appointment, you should definitely discuss it thoroughly beforehand.

My dog's eyes were bulging, the whites of his eyes were red, and his cheeks were swollen, so I had a CT scan scheduled by his vet to investigate the cause.

The appointment was at 10 AM, and the parking lot didn't open until about 15 minutes beforehand, so arriving early didn't allow entry.

First, a nurse asked about my dog's condition and recent activities, and then the veterinarian asked more detailed questions.

I was given explanations about the risks of general anesthesia, the possibility of sudden changes in condition, and the possibility of the scan data being made public for veterinary research.

The CT scan itself took about an hour from the start of anesthesia until the dog recovered.

There were large and small dogs in the waiting room, but because it was by appointment only, it wasn't crowded and was quiet, separate from the cat area.

The results showed that the size of the cheekbone lines below each eye was different.

Inflammation can cause eye bulging, swelling, and pain.

Therefore, a biopsy was performed to examine the cells from that area for pathological testing.

If it's a tumor, radiation therapy will be administered.
If it's inflammation, antibiotics will be given.

The results will be available in two weeks.

Finally, the woman with glasses at the reception desk was very polite and kind.

I'm giving it 4 stars because of the high price.
Isn't it incredibly poorly done for a patellar luxation to re-dislocate when the stitches are removed during suture removal?

He is a trustworthy doctor.
The clinic is clean.
The facilities were clean and the service was excellent.
This is a very good veterinary hospital for dogs.

A veterinarian specializing in that field will diagnose your pet with care and provide a detailed explanation. I was glad I came because I now clearly understand the nature of the illness.

Appointments can only be made through a referral from your regular veterinary clinic. The fees are quite high, and some people have paid exorbitant treatment costs. The cost varies depending on the treatment method, and I think it requires a strong desire to cure your pet and the owner's commitment.

I was taking my child to a local hospital for excessive thirst and urination.

After various tests, the cause remained unknown, so I was referred to this hospital and underwent a CT scan.

The CT scan also found no abnormalities.

However, the doctor's explanations before and after the examination were very clear and reassuring, and my worries were relieved.

I am grateful for the suggestions on future management.

The doctor and staff were all very kind, and it was well worth the long trip.
I went to the vet for my pet on a weekday. They gave me a clear explanation, and the surgery is scheduled for next week.

They explained everything to me very carefully, but the initial consultation fee was ¥11,000! They didn't do any treatment, they didn't give me any medicine, they just listened to my story. There's a veterinary hospital nearby that doesn't charge for just listening to my story, and there are always long lines. I think it would be great if they did.
By the way, the CT scan costs ¥90,000, and the blood test costs ¥11,000.
The vet was very good.

Dr. Oji performed surgery on my dog ​​for a cervical disc herniation.

Dr. Oji is a very calm and kind doctor, and his explanations were thorough and easy to understand, so I felt at ease and confident entrusting my dog ​​to him.

Before the surgery, my dog ​​could barely stand or walk, but immediately after discharge, he was back to his healthy self.

There may have been warning signs, but I didn't notice them, and the symptoms suddenly became severe. It was heartbreaking to watch, knowing there was nothing I could do, but now he's back to his former healthy self, and I'm truly filled with gratitude to the doctor.

I had the impression that dog surgery was extremely expensive, but that wasn't the case, which I was also grateful for.

If there are any dog ​​owners out there whose beloved dogs are suffering like mine, I would definitely recommend this hospital.

The hospital is clean, well-maintained, and equipped with the latest facilities. Not only the doctor, but also the nurses and all the staff (I don't know their titles) were incredibly kind and understanding, truly empathetic to the feelings of pet owners.

Thank you so much.

At the forefront of pet medicine
Equipped with the latest medical equipment, they can treat a wide range of pet illnesses.

I'm glad I took my dog ​​here.
My 9-year-old Chihuahua had an 11cm tumor removed from his liver cancer.
I thought it might not work, but I decided to give it a try anyway and made an appointment.
After a CT scan, the doctor said everything was fine, so the surgery was performed.
It's been less than a month since the surgery, and seeing him able to eat even though he could barely eat at all before is truly grateful.
I'm also grateful to the dog who gave him the blood transfusion!
Thank you very much.

We brought our 10-year-old Chihuahua (with heart disease) to this clinic.

A 9cm tumor was found in her liver, and other clinics had even discussed palliative care, indicating a critical situation.

Here, they performed a CT scan and contrast imaging to carefully assess the possibility of surgery.

Although it was a very high-risk surgery, the doctors never gave up and persevered until the end. As a result, the tumor was completely removed, and there was no metastasis.

Her post-operative recovery was surprisingly quick, and she is now doing well.

[Costs]
・CT + contrast imaging: Approximately 160,000 yen
・Surgery + hospitalization: Approximately 900,000 yen
・Total: Approximately 1,060,000 yen

While it's certainly not cheap, considering the procedure, risks, and outcome, it's completely justifiable.

We are deeply grateful for their advanced medical equipment and skills, and their strong commitment to saving our dog.

We were also grateful for the videos they sent us via LINE during her hospitalization, which allowed us to keep track of her condition.

We would highly recommend this hospital to other pet owners facing similar challenges.
High level

We were referred to this clinic by our regular veterinarian for glaucoma treatment in our dog, but unfortunately, we experienced many unreliable treatments, which made us very uneasy about continuing treatment. The points we found particularly problematic are as follows:

① Excessive "excision" suggestions: Although we were treating our dog with eye drops, the eye pressure didn't decrease as expected, and at each visit, we were strongly advised to "excise the eye." Lacking knowledge, we wondered if this was the best course of action, but after seeking a second opinion from another ophthalmologist, we found that the eye pressure improved with simple treatment without excision, and our dog is now healthy. The thought of having chosen excision at that time is terrifying.

② Inconsistent and confusing statements: The doctor's explanations changed with each visit, and there were numerous instances where completely different instructions were given.
For example, we were told, "Use eye drops A only when symptom XX appears," but at the next visit, we were told, "Didn't I say to use them daily?" There was a lack of consistency. Both my family and I heard these statements, and we recorded each visit for family reference, so this was not a misunderstanding. Furthermore, regarding the incident where the eye drops were not administered due to a misunderstanding in instructions, I overheard nurses speaking ill of me in the back room, which was extremely unpleasant.

Based on these experiences, I have concluded that I cannot trust this hospital. There are other ophthalmologists in Osaka who are more attentive and trustworthy, and I strongly recommend seeking them out.

While I regret not going to this hospital sooner, I hope that other animals and their families will not have to go through the same experience.

I received excellent care for my glaucoma surgery. The initial diagnosis revealed I was already blind, so I underwent surgery to lower my intraocular pressure. As explained beforehand, the post-operative treatment went smoothly without any problems. Although various possibilities were explained before the surgery, I believe the fact that the treatment was completed without complications is a testament to the doctor's skill. Thank you very much.

This is a very clean and pleasant hospital. There's a designated area outside for dogs to relieve themselves, and water is available. There are also cute hooks for leashes scattered throughout the hospital. I was surprised to see that the waiting areas for dogs and cats are separated, showing consideration for each other's privacy.

The doctor explained everything carefully and in detail, which was very helpful.

My dog ​​developed cataracts, so I rushed to a veterinary hospital that specializes in ophthalmology, where they performed surgery right away. 

I was told that there are only a limited number of ophthalmologists at veterinary hospitals, even in Japan. They were able to perform the surgery quickly here, and my dog's eyesight has not worsened or become blind.
Kind

Everyone was purely businesslike.
Dr. Kabe followed the textbook exactly and seemed completely unable to understand what I was saying. Despite Dr. Kabe contracting COVID-19 and the receptionist unilaterally changing my appointment over the phone, during the actual consultation, there was no apology whatsoever; everything was handled in a detached, businesslike manner, and then I was presented with an exorbitant bill.
I will never go there again.
This was the first time I've ever encountered such a hospital.
It's very disappointing.
Animals can't say anything, so it's truly heartbreaking.
There are many staff members there to make money, but I seriously doubt whether any of them consider the feelings of the animals.
I have serious doubts.
They provide thorough diagnoses.

My doctor told me I had cancer, so I went for a CT scan for further testing. Before the scan, he reassured me that it might just be an infection, but when the CT scan came back, it was cancer. How can that happen? I could understand if it was the other way around, but he's family, and it's incredibly sad, so to build me up only to drop me like that is just awful.

Two years ago, we had our 6-month-old Chihuahua undergo portosystemic shunt surgery here.

Thanks to that, our dog is now running around happily and enjoying life to the fullest.

Thank you, Dr. Morishita.

The doctor's explanations were thorough, and he was very kind, choosing his words carefully to be supportive of the owner.

He was so kind even to the owner, so I imagine he's even more attentive to everyone's pets.

He explains things in an easy-to-understand way, including the risks of surgery, the risks of not having surgery, and other treatment options.

He allows you to make a decision after hearing everything, which I think is very honest.

You should be able to make a decision you're comfortable with.

He also explained what our dog was like immediately after the surgery, and then let us see him for a few minutes.

Our dog was probably groggy and won't remember, but I was so happy to see him, even for a moment, as I thought I wouldn't be able to see him from the surgery until he was discharged.

He shows a lot of thoughtful consideration in trying to alleviate the anxieties of pet owners.


My pet was hospitalized for about a week, and for various reasons, visits were not permitted. However, during that time, they sent daily reports via their official LINE account, including a short 15-second video and a brief explanation of how my pet was doing.

Even though they were busy, the fact that they took the time to do this shows that they not only treat illnesses but also genuinely care for us pet owners. It was a wonderful hospital.

When I picked my pet up, I was surprised to see how attached he had become to the nurses, but I think it's proof of the love and care they put into caring for my pet.

Regarding phone service, there's one very experienced and communicative person, but when others answered, the service was a bit sloppy.

I called to confirm the final payment on the morning of the day I picked up my pet, but for some reason, they quoted me the price excluding tax.

The amount quoted on the phone and the amount quoted on pickup were different, which was confusing.

Since the final payment is inclusive of tax, I think they should always quote the price including tax.

The amount isn't cheap, after all.

The reception staff weren't directly involved in my pet's illness, but their service in other areas was excellent.

We received care for our dog in December 2022 🐶. We were given only one month to live, so our goal was for her to reach her 12th birthday. Thanks to Dr. Une, Ms. Maeda, and the other wonderful nurses, she was able to celebrate her 14th birthday in good health at the end of March 2025! She's so energetic every day, it's hard to believe she's an old dog! She eats lots of food and treats, walks a lot, and sleeps well 😊! She's started to get startled and fall over often, but she quickly gets up and walks briskly 🐾. We were able to see her like this in her later years thanks to this hospital 🙇‍♀️. Our whole family is grateful! Thank you so much! 😆

I met a truly wonderful teacher.

Thank you so much.

About 13 years ago, I was referred to a local doctor because they couldn't treat my dog's condition of unknown cause, and he was admitted as an emergency patient.
I think there's a good and bad doctor involved.
Even after he was released from the hospital, my dog ​​continued to scream in pain, so I got worried and called Neovets,
but they were very cold and just asked me, "What kind of tests do you want me to do?"
I never want to use their services again.
Even though I told them the pain seemed severe, they didn't even prescribe any anti-inflammatory medication.

My dog ​​is a large breed, and no vet could figure out the cause of his condition. We finally got him diagnosed at NeoVets VR Center, and he's recovered after surgery.

I'm truly grateful to the head veterinarian. It's a really great hospital!

I visited this clinic on a referral from my regular vet to discuss cataract surgery for my 13-year-old miniature dachshund. The parking lot is spacious and seems to accommodate about 10 cars. It's by appointment only, and the medical questionnaire can be completed online. The spacious waiting room is clean and has an interior that immediately suggests it's a high-quality hospital, making you forget it's an animal hospital. It felt more like a hospital for a human health checkup. The female veterinarian examined my dog ​​carefully and explained each test slowly and thoroughly using models, so there was nothing I didn't understand. Because it's by appointment only, it's not a rushed hospital where they see patients one after another, so they were able to patiently answer any questions or concerns I had. I had researched canine cataracts to some extent, but I wasn't worried about being pressured into surgery. In this case, my dog's chances of seeing after surgery were low, and considering the risks, we decided against surgery. The explanation was very thorough and I was satisfied with the diagnosis. There were no unnecessary tests, which gave me peace of mind. The doctor was kind and calm, without any condescending or arrogant opinions, and gave an unbiased explanation. I could feel that he was truly attentive to our needs. What surprised me the most was that when pets feel safe with the doctor at the animal hospital, they don't tremble, get out of breath, or become agitated. It's the same at our regular vet, but I don't know what pets are deciding, but they seem to calm down when they feel they can trust the doctor. I also researched the costs beforehand, so I went after seeing the average price for an eye checkup, and I didn't get the impression that the bill was excessively high. They also offered credit card and other payment options, which was reassuring. I also learned a lot about what canine cataracts are. It was an expensive checkup, but the explanation was so thorough that it felt like I had attended a kind of educational session. This time, my dog ​​couldn't have cataract surgery and only had an examination, but I was satisfied with the diagnosis and felt positive about finding ways to enjoy life together even if he can't see. Unlike human hospitals, animal hospitals often seem to charge exorbitant fees. That's why I think it's important to choose a hospital where you can be seen by a doctor you trust and feel confident in. I felt that this hospital was trustworthy. Thank you!

I took my cat to the vet for an eye examination.

The building is new, spacious, and clean, and it seems to have all the necessary diagnostic equipment, including X-ray machines.

There's also a second floor, and the vet gave me a thorough explanation. Fortunately, surgery wasn't necessary, and I was prescribed oral medication and eye drops. I'll be going back for a second check-up.

Incidentally, all the tests were done, and the total cost without insurance was 54,000 yen.

I don't know all the staff, but I think this is a hospital with a well-organized and well-equipped system.
Anyone who thinks the fees are unreasonably high should go to another family doctor.
This is a secondary care hospital.
The fee was completely reasonable.

I'm reposting this with added pre- and post-operative photos (videos and pictures).

My dog ​​underwent surgery for a Grade 5 herniated disc (the most severe type of intervertebral disc herniation).

I was filled with anxiety about whether my dog ​​could withstand general anesthesia, whether he would ever walk again, and whether the surgery would be successful. However, the staff were incredibly kind and helpful, and I felt completely at ease entrusting him to their care.

Because it was an urgent situation, he was admitted to the hospital on the day of the examination and underwent surgery the following morning.

He was hospitalized for about a week, and I received daily videos and messages via LINE showing his condition, which was very reassuring.

Upon discharge, I received a lovely hospital diary with pictures of my dog.

The total cost was 650,000 yen.

The medical care provided was well worth the cost.

I am truly grateful to all the staff.

I am filled with gratitude for the attentive care I received.

The following is an update:

Seven months have passed since the surgery.

Although she had paralysis in both lower limbs and lost deep pain sensation, she recovered enough to run around within a month after surgery.

She occasionally loses her balance and stumbles, but seeing her run around so energetically still fills me with emotion, as I never thought she would ever walk again.

She also gradually gained control of her urination, and was able to stop wearing diapers after about two months.

My dog ​​underwent anterior cruciate ligament rupture surgery (TPLO) a month ago, referred by our regular veterinarian, and we continue to visit the clinic monthly. He can now go for walks, and we take him early in the morning because of the heat. The doctor and nurses are very kind and explain things clearly. (P.S.) It's almost been six months since the surgery, and he can now walk normally, although he sometimes pulls on the leash during walks, which is a bit of a challenge. He's an indoor dog and runs around the house. The surgery was expensive, but seeing my son's (my dog's) smile and his healthy appearance makes me glad we had the surgery, and I'm grateful to the doctor and nurses.

Just a consultation, no treatment, and a very condescending attitude, costing over 40,000 yen.
There are plenty of other good places.

My dog ​​developed a tumor on its spleen, so my regular vet referred us to this hospital, and despite the distance, we chose to have our dog treated here.

The doctors and nurses were incredibly kind and thorough, explaining everything clearly, including the pre-operative CT scan, explanations, and costs.

This hospital seems to focus mainly on surgery, as it seems to treat many dogs with serious health issues. Things proceed rather matter-of-factly (not in a bad way), but seeing the doctor made me feel at ease and confident in their care.

However, the fees are quite high.

Perhaps it's because the facilities and doctors are highly professional. 😂 In our case, the contrast-enhanced CT scan was 110,000 yen, and the surgery was 600,000 to 700,000 yen.

I just have to accept that the money will somehow work itself out once my dog ​​gets better. 😂

Yesterday, we found out that our dog's tumor was benign, and I truly feel that having the surgery here was the right decision.
The doctor was kind and thorough, and the clinic was very clean, which was great!

I have a 9-year-old French Bulldog, and we've visited this clinic twice for a lumbar herniated disc and a cervical herniated disc.

There are about 15 parking spaces available, and I've used them every time, but I've never seen them full.

However, there doesn't seem to be a bicycle parking area.

The clinic is kept very clean, and the corridors and waiting area are spacious, with ample room even when using a stroller.

Both the lumbar and cervical herniated discs were diagnosed accurately, and my dog ​​recovered well.

For the cervical herniated disc, surgery was performed, and the explanation was thorough, allowing me to entrust my dog ​​to them with peace of mind.

During the post-operative hospitalization, in addition to daily visits, the nurses also provided updates via LINE.

While it is expensive due to it being a secondary referral service and the nature of the treatment, it is a hospital that provides appropriate medical care for dogs.

It's located in the city center, but it's easy to use as it has ample parking.

The doctors, nurses, and reception staff are all very kind. …

I went there on a referral from my regular hospital.
They have a specialist department, so I went to the ophthalmology department. …

I previously received treatment at this hospital for the removal of an oral tumor. The explanations were thorough and easy to understand, and there were no problems after the surgery. During my hospital stay, I was able to relax in a …

This is a veterinary hospital specializing in secondary care. To visit, you need a referral from your family doctor.
They performed surgery to repair and strengthen the broken plate on my dog's …
The doctors and nurses are all highly skilled and provide accurate diagnoses.
